newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bond yields headed south again on Tuesday as local short-covering, good offshore interest and a stronger U.S. Treasury bond hauled the market nearly 20-basis points lower.
At 1400 GMT, the benchmark R150 gilt was pegged at a 14.70 percent yield having started the day at 14.87 percent and traded as low as 14.69 percent.
Short-covering in the wake of a better-than-expected March private sector credit extension figure was cited as the initial reason for the market's buoyant mood.
Dealers said the market had approached the data, which also showed March M3 above market expectations, with the view that the possibility of a rate hike this year had receded.

Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said ahead of the data's release on Friday that recent trends in credit and money supply growth begged the question whether current monetary policy was restrictive enough.
His comments triggered a selloff which pushed yields up to 14.90 percent on Friday.

But dealers said the fact that growth in credit extension to the private sector increased 15.96 percent, below a consensus forecast of a 16.50 percent rise, had girded the previous week's sellers to buy back their stock.
The market was also bolstered by good offshore buying, which dealers said appeared to be linked to hedging on two new Eurorand issues.
"We've seen some good foreign buying which could have had something to do with hedging on the zero-coupons which triggered stop losses on the R150," a trader said.
Earlier, Bank Nederlandse Gemeenten set a 2.5 billion rand 2017 bond and a 4.0 billion rand 2020 bond.

Later in the day, the U.S. Treasury bond also lent a hand as the yield on the 30-year bond plunged to a 7.01 percent yield from 7.13 percent before the release of data which dealers said had reduced pressure on the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates next month.
The U.S. employment cost index rose 0.6 percent in the first quarter against forecasts of a 0.9 percent rise, while March durable goods orders fell 3.0 percent against predictions of a flat number.
The data helped the R150 down from 14.76 percent to its intraday low of 14.69 percent where dealers said options-related selling ahead of Friday's close-out steadied the market.
Dealers said that on Wednesday the market would focus on events on the U.S. market in the absence of any local indicators and expected the R150 to trade in a 14.75 to 14.65 percent range.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners were net buyers of 679.9 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday after buying 198.09 million rand's worth on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 8.18 billion rand on Friday from 36.48 billion rand on Thursday -- settlement day.
